analysis.title: Market Internal Insight: Systematic Selling Exhausted; Real Money Support Points to Recovery
key_insights: UBS estimates Risk Control funds turn to buyers on Tuesday (+$10-15 bn) after two days of heavy systematic selling, and says CTA selling is largely complete with limited incremental impact from here.
The desk expects a potentially quieter Tuesday ahead of the midterm election, with scope for a recovery starting Wednesday after the election.

Friday systematic selling was estimated at ~$130-150 bn: CTA $70-80 bn, Risk Control $30-40 bn, Leveraged ETFs $30 bn. Nasdaq excess flow was -$8 bn versus -$24 bn in the S&P 500, because most CTA sell triggers were in the S&P 500.

Monday (Nov 2) systematic selling was estimated at ~$85-115 bn: Risk Control $65-85 bn, CTA $10-15 bn, Leveraged ETFs $10-15 bn. Excess flow was -$16 bn in the S&P 500 and -$53 bn in Nasdaq, where most CTA and Leveraged ETF selling and some Risk Control deleveraging was concentrated.

Real money bought the dip on all three down days: UBS RMM clients bought all 3 days, foreign-listed US ETFs bought all 3 days, and Multi-Asset Managers / Risk Parity bought on Monday as equity/bond correlation turned negative.

Most Monday selling came after 1:30pm in orderly, steady flow that mimics systematic selling. S&P 500 excess flow was +$15 bn until 1:30pm then -$31 bn to the close. Nasdaq was -$4 bn until 1:30pm then -$49 bn.

UBS RMM net flow was at the 62nd percentile versus 3 years after being as low as the 28th percentile at 10:05am. Tax-loss harvesting continued, with selling in Tech (semis, hardware, IT services) and buying of ETFs (mostly SGOV, QQQ and VOO), plus a buy tilt in Software.

The Risk Control sell estimate for Monday was cut to $65-85 bn because more Risk Control funds moved to intraday rebalancing on Friday. After Tuesday's rebalance, Risk Control exposure would be 97%, the 69th percentile versus 1 year and 86th versus 5 years.
One-month equity/bond correlation fell to -46%, which suggests Treasuries act as a risk-off asset again. UBS sees no sign of a Risk Parity unwind in this sell-off.

CTA global equity exposure is 12% after Monday's rebalance, at the 9th percentile versus 1 year and 32nd versus 5 years. Some funds may sell about 50 bps before the model triggers, so UBS expects limited further CTA sell impact even though the model NQ1 trigger is 28050.2 and the ES1 trigger is 7556.5.
Leveraged ETPs sold -$12 bn on Monday, all in QQQ and tech exposure. The top 10 stocks to sell by dollar amount are NVDA, MU, AMD, AVGO, INTC, AAPL, MSFT, TXN, ADI and MRVL.
Corporate buybacks are in low seasonality this week and next, then enter high seasonality of +$35-55 bn per week starting the week of Nov 16.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Negative correlation means Treasuries act as a risk-off asset again, so diversification works for multi-asset managers and Risk Parity is not unwinding.

CTA sell triggers remain close: ES1 at 7556.5 (-0.3%) and NQ1 at 28050.2 (-0.5%), plus an NQ1 MT MA crossover expected later this week.
Buybacks are in low seasonality for the next two weeks, so there is less corporate bid support until the week of Nov 16.
Nasdaq and tech carry concentrated systematic and leveraged ETF selling.

tension_points.bull_case: Risk Control turns to buyers (+$10-15 bn) on Tuesday and CTA selling is largely complete. Retail, foreign investors and multi-asset managers bought the dip on all three down days, and equity/bond correlation is back to negative.
tension_points.bear_case: A further SPX drop would force Risk Control selling of -$60-65 bn at -1.5% and -$110-120 bn at -2%. CTA triggers sit close (ES1 7556.5, NQ1 28050.2), and buybacks stay in low seasonality for two weeks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SPX falling 1.5% or more on Tuesday, which would put Risk Control back to selling -$60-65 bn or more.
